name: Ultrasonic Reflections by Abel Korinsky
description:
Join us for the final presentation of Abel Korinsky, bangaloREsident@TheISRO, before he heads back to Germany!

During his residency at The Indian Sonic Research Organisation, Korinsky explored the sonic “heritage” of Bangalore, identifying the residues of sounds around us as the city’s sonic landscape shifts.

Ultrasonic Reflections is a work in progress that takes ambisonic and field recordings from Bangalore and transforms them into a spatial sonic experience. A 16-channel audio system creates the main musical and atmospheric layer, surrounding the audience with sounds caught from the city. The recordings are transformed until their original sources are hardly recognisable, while still reflecting the atmosphere, intensity, and contrasts that he experienced during his stay in Bangalore.

Friday, October 16, 8:00 pm onwards

The Indian Sonic Research Organisation

Entry free. Open to all.

name: Fossil Hunting Expedition - Ariyalur Cretaceous Coast
description:
**Around 70–100 million years ago, South India’s coastline ran through what is now Ariyalur, Tamil Nadu. A warm, shallow sea covered the land, home to ammonites, sea snails, oysters, sea urchins and sharks. When these animals died, they sank into the seabed and were buried in mud and lime. Over millions of years, these layers hardened into rock, while the sea retreated and the seabed became land.**

**Today, monsoon rains expose fossils across Ariyalur’s gullies and ravines, making it one of India’s richest fossil regions. The area has also yielded dinosaur bones and eggs.**

Above Zenith’s first fossil hunting expedition. Over one weekend, you will hunt for fossils at two sites with geologists and paleontologists, learn how to identify and record what you find, and take your finds home.

**What you might find:**

**Ammonites, Belemnites, Gastropods, Bivalves & oysters, Sea urchins, Fossilised wood and Shark teeth.**

**Highlights:**

1. Two fossil hunting sessions, at a younger and an older rock formation
2. A fossil museum visit to see the region's best specimens
3. A limestone mine or cement plant visit (subject to permission)
4. A personal fossil hunting kit to keep
5. A geology session on reading rock layers and identifying your finds
6. A review of the weekend's finds with the resource people
7. Gangaikonda Cholapuram, a 11th century Chola temple and UNESCO World Heritage Site

**Itinerary:**

**Day 0 · Friday, 16 October**

From Bangalore, we drive overnight to Ariyalur.

**Day 1 · Saturday, 17 October**

**Fossil Hunt 1 · 8:45 am to 10:45 am**

**Fossil museum · 11:15 am to 12:45 pm**

**Geology session · 4:30 pm to 6:30 pm**

**Day 2 · Sunday, 18 October**

**Fossil Hunt 2 · 6:15 am to 9:15 am**

**Finds review · 11:00 am to 12:30 pm**

**Limestone mine or cement plant · 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm**

**Gangaikonda Cholapuram · 4:15 pm to 6:00 pm**

**Dinner and departure**

**Day 3 · Monday, 19 October**

Drop-offs between 4:30 am and 5:30 am

This trip is open to all ages: families, kids and adults. No background in science is needed, just curiosity.

name: Improv 101: How Not to Panic on Stage | Workshop by Improv Lore
description:
Most people think improvisers are fearless; the truth is they've simply learned what to do when they don't know what to do.

This beginner-friendly introduction to improv is designed for anyone who's ever worried about saying the wrong thing, running out of ideas, or freezing up in front of others. Through fun games, simple exercises, and guided scene work, you'll learn how to trust your instincts, embrace uncertainty, and stay present when things don't go according to plan.

Throughout the course, you'll explore the core principles of improvisation, collaborative storytelling, and spontaneous creativity in a supportive, low-pressure environment.

No acting or stage experience is required. You don't need to be funny, quick-witted, or confident. All you need is a willingness to step on stage and discover that you're capable of more than you think.

**Schedule**

*This course runs over four consecutive days:﻿*

• Saturday, October 17 - 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM

• Sunday, October 18 - 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM

• Monday, October 19 - 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM

• Tuesday, October 20 - 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM

A special Graduation Show is tentatively planned for Sunday, November 1, from 11:00 AM to 12:30 PM. The audience will consist exclusively of friends and family, creating a supportive environment for participants taking the stage for the first time.

**Who Are Improv Lore?**

Improv Lore is a Bangalore-based community theatre troupe dedicated to spreading the art of spontaneous storytelling and unscripted performance while rekindling the joy of playfulness and creativity. The community gathers regularly for improv jams, workshops, and collaborative learning experiences. 🎭✨

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Travels in a Ceramic Tea Cup
description:
Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

Tea is ubiquitous and it is the beverage of choice for people across the world.

Drunk green, black or with milk or butter. sometimes sweet, unsweetened or salty, it is sipped in the quiet of the morning, during an office break and even for a 100 kilometre drive. Tea is both luxurious and humble.

The culture of drinking tea overlaps with the culture of ceramics which are used for brewing, pouring and drinking.

This lecture brings together the material history of tea drinking and the cultures of art, architecture, design and ceramics that have grown with it.

**About the Speaker**

Annapurna Garimella is an art historian and a designer. Her research focuses on late medieval Indic architecture and the history and practices of vernacular visual and built cultures in India after Independence. She is the Managing Trustee of Art, Resources and Teaching Trust, which has a research library and conducts independent research and teaching. She also heads Jackfruit Research and Design, an organisation with a specialised portfolio of design, research, and curation. Most recently, Garimella has developed and taught the online course “A History of Indian Craft: 1850s to the Present” for MAP Academy.

Her newest book is The Long Arc of South Asian Art: A Reader in Honor of Vidya Dehejia (Women Unlimited, 2022).

Designing India: 1947 to the Present, an edited volume; A Face on a Face: South Asian Masks in the Vaidya Collection; and Digesting the Past: The Discourse of Sacralized Architectural Renovation in Southern India (14th-17th Centuries) are book manuscripts under preparation.

**Event Details**

📅 Saturday, 17 October

🕛 2 PM – 4 PM

📍 Atta Galatta, Indiranagar, Bengaluru

**Your ticket includes:**

• 1 complimentary kombucha from Umami Brew

• First-come, first-served seating

**About Pint of View**

Pint of View is India's Largest Lecture Community. We brought the lecture in bar format to India and are now expanding across the globe with chapters in 14 cities worldwide. Here, big ideas meet intimate spaces, and you walk in curious and walk out with a sharper lens on the world.

Book now and develop your own pint of view. 🍻

name: The Analog Club: Halloween Edition
description:
Step back in time at **The Analog Club: Halloween Edition,** an event series by the Studio by Copper + Cloves.

*Imagine walking into a busy cafe and seeing not a single phone, no one taking selfies, and no one around you scrolling — just people dressed up, chatting, creating, reading, and enjoying being present.*

Disconnect from devices for 3 hours of unplugged time — we'll have books, board games, music, crochet, and, of course, spooky-themed food! But this isn't about structured activities or organised fun, just genuine connection and relaxation. The event will be fluid — you can dip into activities if you want, chat to new people, graze at our high tea counter, or get creative at our Halloween-themed art corner.

And because it’s Halloween, **your best costume is a MUST!** 👻 Come dressed up, get into the spirit, and make the most of our spooky little corner of the analog world.

Meet new friends, sketch, or read a book in quiet solitude (without being surrounded by people lost in their phones).

Embrace the analog experience, slow down, and reconnect in this crazy digital age — with a little Halloween magic.

**Info:**

Strictly no devices (no laptops or iPads, and you will be asked to keep your phone in a basket or in your bag—not in your pocket or on a table. E-books are allowed). We will not be using social media on our phones at the event; at times, we will only take photos with a camera.

Tickets are for entry, all games and art supplies, Halloween-themed food, and unlimited high tea from our renowned deli counter. Do not purchase a ticket if you are unwilling to surrender your devices for 3 hours.

name: Indiranagar Code Walk!
description:
🌸 Indiranagar Code Walk

**A relaxed 2-hour walk through Indiranagar where you'll explore the neighborhood and turn what you see into small pieces of code-art.**

No coding experience needed. We'll guide you every step of the way.

**What will we do?**

We'll walk to a few spots in Indiranagar and pause at each one. At every stop, you'll:

1. **Listen** to a short story or local anecdote about the place and its people.
2. **Observe** the colors, shapes, and sounds around you.
3. **Code** a small sketch in **p5.js** (a beginner-friendly creative coding tool) inspired by what you noticed. You'll start with a simple template and make it your own.

By the end, you'll have a handful of code-art pieces that capture your own impressions of the neighborhood.

**What to bring**

- 💻 A laptop (Mac, Windows, or Linux), fully charged
- 📱 A phone
- 👟 Comfortable shoes and clothes, as there's light walking involved

name: Side A/Side B: Disco Jazz by Rupa
description:
Calgary, winter of 1981. **Rupa Biswas**, a young singer from Calcutta, steps into a studio with a sarod maestro and a Canadian disco band, and two weeks later **Disco Jazz** exists.

It sold a handful of copies, slipped away for forty years, and came back when *Aaj Shanibar* found a million listeners on YouTube.

A record this full of warmth deserves a proper Sunday evening, so come spend this one with us.

This listening session is hosted by **Ketan Bahira**t (Oceantied), a Bangalore producer and DJ since 2014, Red Bull Music Academy alum, with sets at Dimensions and Magnetic Fields, and **Tanisha Thyagarajan** (DoubleT), a textile designer whose sets move through UK Funky, Jersey Club, Brazilian Funk and footwork.

description:

In this session, we will together explore how you can make a top that you can wear as you like. Away from standard measurement templates, we will instead think with the body and unpack what (fun)ctionality in clothes can feel like and offer.

As we engage in this session, you will also learn the basics of pattern making, seam work, and garment construction, all while making the process yours and only yours.

Beginners are welcome.

All material will be provided.

name: Gatecrash presents CKRAFT and ManeatingOrchid
description:
**About CKRAFT:**

CKRAFT blends the crushing force of **Metal** with the eccentric freedom of **Jazz**. Led by accordionist Charles Kieny, the quintet sets a Meshuggah inspired power trio (guitar, bass, drums) against the frantic breath of a tenor saxophone and a cyborg-accordion augmented with electronic sensors.

Medieval polyphonies, and other thousand years old melodies — roots of Western music — collide with modern creativity, opening a space for enriching cross-cultural dialogue with the Indian audience.

**LINE-UP**

Charles Kieny (augmented accordion)

Théo Nguyen Duc Long (saxophone)

Antoine Morisot (guitar)

Marc Karapetian (bass)

William Bur (drums)

**About ManeatingOrchid:**

Formed in 2011, ManeatingOrchid has spent over a decade shaping a sound that fuses prog metal, mathcore, and extreme music into something chaotic and unpredictable. Known for dense riffing, abrasive vocals, and constantly shifting song structures, the band has become one of the subcontinent’s most uncompromising heavy acts.Their self-titled 2016 EP earned cult acclaim within the underground, while Miasma (2019) and Hive Mind (2022) pushed their sound further into dissonant, volatile territory — cementing Maneating Orchid as a band that consistently defies convention.

**The Humming Tree:**

The Humming Tree - A grassroots performance venue in Bangalore, running from 2013 to 2019 and in the process becoming a cornerstone of Bangalore’s independent music, art, and cultural ecosystem.

Now, in 2026, The Humming Tree is back in a brand-new, purpose-designed space in Indiranagar. Built across 12,000 sq. ft., the venue features a 600+ capacity performance space, world-class sound and lighting systems, and a diverse F&B proposition. More than just a venue, it’s a hub for creativity, culture and collaboration.

name: Dakshin Diaries by The Counterpoint Crew
description:
Dakshin Diaries by The Counterpoint Crew brings a fresh, contemporary choral experience to the proscenium stage. Featuring 20 voices delivering live amplified stage harmony, this concert explores distinct musical worlds without creative boundaries.

The performance showcases a brand-new repertoire spanning classical polyphony, soulful regional folk, and iconic melodies reimagined across Kannada, Tamil, Hindi, Malayalam, Telugu, and English. Audiences will experience rich vocal arrangements alongside independent music. Every piece is thoughtfully arranged to celebrate the expressive versatility and dynamic resonance of the human voice.

Designed as an immersive, seated auditorium showcase, the evening offers music lovers a rare opportunity to hear diverse genres unified through rich, multi-part choral textures. Whether you are a dedicated choral enthusiast, an indie music follower, or simply seeking an evocative musical evening, take your seat and let the harmony surround you.

name: DIY Camera Obscura
description:
Build & Experiment with a Handmade Pinhole Camera

Long before lenses and megapixels, there was the *camera obscura*—a simple box, a pinhole, and the magic of light painting an image. In this workshop with artist **Stuti Bansal**, you’ll make your own camera obscura from scratch, explore the principles of analogue image-making, and develop unique photographs using light-sensitive paper.

**You’ll get to:**

- Build your own **working camera obscura**
- Learn the science & history behind the camera obscura
- Experiment with capturing and developing images
- Take home your handmade camera + prints you create

**Who is it for?**

Artists, photographers, makers, students, and anyone curious about analog photography and light-based art. No prior experience required.
